_README: SAMPLE DATA. Made-up prices in the Atlas ladder format so the app and tests run. Not real buyer prices. Put your buyer's sheet in with scripts/refresh_atlas.py.

deduction_flags.verbatim: Cracked Back = $75 off / Cracked Lens = $75 off / Bad Face ID = Parts / Bad Back Camera = ASK - - - HEAVY SCRATCHING / DEGRADED BATTERY % / Repair Message(s) = EXTRA DEDUCTION
deduction_flags.battery_under_80: Atlas's rules block lists 'DEGRADED BATTERY % = EXTRA DEDUCTION' with NO printed threshold on the 2026-09-04 tab. The '<80%' figure carried by older versions of this file is NOT stated on the current sheet -- the 80 in server.py is our own trigger, not Atlas's. Treat a degraded battery as an unquantified deduction riding on top of the grade column.
deduction_flags.bad_esn: CARRIED FORWARD from the 2026-07-29 read and NOT re-verified on the 2026-09-04 tab -- treat as unconfirmed. Accepted if NOT stolen. 'Unlocked Relocks / KG Lock - NO TIME LIMIT': if status flips after sale, SELLER is liable for deduction or return. Disclosure, not a floor adjustment.
deduction_flags.cracked_back: $75 off on the USED tab. The Parts/iC tab carries its own SMALLER per-model cracked-back deductions (16 Pro Max -$75, 12 Pro Max -$75). Two different tabs, two different numbers -- do not mix them.
deduction_flags.bad_face_id: Routes to Parts, not a grade deduction.
deduction_flags.aftermarket_screen: 'Aftermarket (AM) Screen = Bad LCD', and Bad LCD caps the unit at Grade D. This is the rule that caps INV-2026-017.
deduction_flags.shipping: FREE FedEx labels at min 5 devices. Deductions/returns fully at Atlas's discretion. No stolen/fraudulent items.

not_on_current_ladder.note: No published ladder row for used MacBooks in this sample.
